Consult Summary:
- 3-day history of watery diarrhea (≈6–7×/day) with episodic left-lower abdominal cramping, initial vomiting, low-grade subjective fever, and weakness after recent Chinese takeaway; no blood in stool.
- Clinical impression of acute gastroenteritis; conservative management with oral rehydration, paracetamol, rest, and review if not improved in 3–4 days.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute watery diarrhea x 3 days, 6–7 bowel motions/day.
- Associated: left-sided lower abdominal crampy pain (intermittent), early self-limited vomiting, subjective fever at onset, weakness/shakiness, reduced appetite; no hematochezia, no ongoing fever, no back radiation.
- Possible food-borne trigger: Chinese restaurant meal 4 days ago; one child vomited only.
- No chronic GI history.
- Impression: Likely viral > bacterial gastroenteritis.

Issue 2:
- Asthma (well-controlled).
- Uses inhaler (type/dose/frequency not documented).
- No recent exacerbations.

Issue 3:
- Occupational/social impact: keeps working as an accountant but needs constant toilet proximity; advised time off work for recovery.

Medications:
- Asthma inhaler (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.

Social History:
- Lives with wife and two children.
- Non-smoker.
- Does not drink alcohol.
- Works as an accountant.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination or vitals recorded.

Plan:
- Conservative management for presumed gastroenteritis:
  • Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) as per packaging.  
  • Maintain adequate fluids; light diet as tolerated.  
  • Paracetamol 2 tablets (dose not specified) up to 4 times daily PRN for fever/discomfort.  
  • Rest and refrain from work for 2–3 days.
- Red flags / follow-up:
  • Return or seek care if no improvement in 3–4 days, worsening symptoms, high fever, blood in stool, or unable to keep fluids down.  
  • If persistent, consider stool culture and further investigations; reassess need for antibiotics.
- Provide sick note if required for employer.
